tasks.short: Ask about health and medicines, enter the answers, check medicines for bleeding and anaesthetic risks, review the history and consult on unclear points.

steps.what: Dental hygienist asks the patient about health, medicines and allergies
Dental hygienist records the patient medical histories in the dental record
Dental hygienist looks up medicines for bleeding risk and interactions with the anaesthetic
Dental hygienist reviews the history for risks before treatment
Dental hygienist asks the dentist or GP about unclear conditions

tasks.design: Patients fill in the health questionnaire in the practice portal before the visit, and the answers land in the dental record ({OTHER}); the hygienist asks follow-up questions instead of the full list. Fixed drug rules in the record flag medicines with bleeding risk or interactions with the local anaesthetic. Reviewing risks and consulting the dentist or GP stay with the hygienist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Histories were asked and typed at every visit, and medicines looked up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice portals feed questionnaires into the record, and drug rule sets flag risks.
tasks.still_hard: Patients forget medicines; the follow-up questions still matter.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a patient on blood thinners who did not mention them.
tasks.altitude: The hygienist reviews a pre-filled history instead of taking it from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether pre-filled histories shorten the start of visits.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates; KNMP sets the content.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
Health data are special category; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit to clarified conditions; treatment is outside.
Input contract: questionnaire filled in by the patient in the portal; drug rules from the national drug database; fallback is asking and typing.
Reviewing and consulting do not change.
Patients' time is outside the hygienist's savings.
unknowns: Share of patients who fill in the questionnaire.
research_questions: Are risk medicines missed less often?

incremental.description: Dental hygienist reads the questionnaire before the visit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patients who skip the questionnaire save nothing on the history.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clean teeth and treat gums, explain home care, send the chosen care instructions and record the treatment.

steps.what: Dental hygienist provides clinical services by cleaning teeth and treating gums
Dental hygienist gives health education on brushing and flossing
Dental hygienist hands out printed care instructions
Dental hygienist records the treatment given

tasks.design: The hygienist ticks the home-care tools and techniques shown in the dental record ({OTHER}), and the practice portal sends the matching fixed instruction sheets and videos to the patient. Treatment codes are picked from lists. Cleaning, treating and teaching stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were printed and treatments typed as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice portals send fixed instruction sheets chosen in the record.
tasks.still_hard: Habits change in the chair, not from sheets.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a patient where the brush keeps missing.

reach.learn: Whether sent videos improve home care.

evidence.claim: Practice portals send fixed instruction sheets and videos chosen in the record.
Health data sent to patients must go through a secure channel.

assumptions: Boundary: from treatment to the recorded treatment; follow-up visits are outside.
Input contract: instruction sheets approved by the practice's hygienists; fallback is printouts.
Treating and teaching do not change.
research_questions: Do bleeding scores improve between visits?

incremental.description: Dental hygienist ticks the tools shown.

approvals.approved_version: The home-care tools and techniques chosen by the hygienist in s2; changes need a new choice before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is treatment in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine teeth and measure pockets, fill in the periodontal chart, mark decay, compare with earlier charts and discuss with the dentist.

steps.what: Dental hygienist examines teeth and measures pocket depths
Dental hygienist writes pocket depths and bleeding points in the periodontal chart
Dental hygienist charts conditions of decay and disease for diagnosis by the dentist
Dental hygienist compares the chart with earlier charts
Dental hygienist discusses the findings with the dentist

tasks.design: Voice-controlled periodontal charting in the dental record ({OTHER}) fills pocket depths and bleeding points as the hygienist speaks them, and the hygienist checks the chart at the end. A comparison view highlights teeth where depths changed since the last visit. Examining, charting decay and discussing with the dentist stay with the hygienist; no AI reads x-rays here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written down or called out to an assistant, and charts compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Voice charting and comparison views are available in dental records.
tasks.still_hard: Speech recognition mishears numbers; the chart must be checked.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling the difference between a deep pocket and calculus.

reach.learn: Whether change views speed up treatment decisions.

evidence.claim: Voice-controlled periodontal charting fills readings into the dental chart.
Providers are responsible for careful use of AI tools: assess risks, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from examining to findings shared; diagnosis by the dentist is outside.
Input contract: earlier charts in the dental record; fallback is writing readings down.
Examining, charting decay and discussing do not change.
Dentist time is outside the hygienist's savings.

already_counted.description: Dental hygienist checks the voice-filled chart.

incremental.description: Dental hygienist trains the voice commands.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is examining in the mouth.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose accredited courses, attend them, get attendance into the quality register and follow points against the requirement.

steps.what: Dental hygienist attends continuing education courses
Dental hygienist uploads certificates to the quality register
Dental hygienist tracks points against the re-registration requirement in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Accredited course providers report attendance directly to the quality register ({PARTNER_PORTAL}), which shows points per domain against the re-registration requirement and lists accredited courses that fill the gaps. Choosing and attending courses stay with the hygienist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Certificates were uploaded by hand and points tracked in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Quality registers take attendance from accredited providers and show points.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing courses that improve care is the hygienist's own judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a course because patients keep asking about a new technique.

reach.learn: Whether provider reporting saves assistants' time.

evidence.claim: Quality registers take attendance from accredited providers and show points per period.
Hygienists in the quality register must meet re-registration points each period.

assumptions: Boundary: from requirements to points status; paying for courses is outside.
Input contract: attendance reported by accredited providers; requirements set by the quality register; fallback is uploading by hand.
Choosing and attending do not change.
Providers that do not report need a manual upload.
research_questions: Do hygienists re-register without last-minute courses?

incremental.description: Dental hygienist checks the register once a quarter.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is attending courses.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The dental hygienist keeps treatment, teaching and clinical judgement; asking, typing and charting by hand shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A hygienist who spends saved minutes coaching patients in the chair.
